## Harden username validation against homograph attacks

Usernames are currently validated with a small ASCII regex. That is fine for ASCII, but we keep seeing signups that abuse look-alike Unicode characters to impersonate existing users (e.g. mixing Latin and Cyrillic). To make the allowed set explicit and auditable, this adds a generated code-point allow-list table and switches `is_valid_username` to consult it.

The table is produced by `gen_allowed.py` (checked in alongside it) and covers code points up to U+04FF; everything outside the allow-list is rejected. Regenerating is a one-liner: `python gen_allowed.py > allowed_table.py`.

### Tests
Existing username tests pass (length bounds, ASCII letters/digits/`-`/`_` accepted; uppercase, spaces and accented characters rejected).

    pytest tests/test_username.py
